articles.title: MHI Invites Global Bids to Build 10 GWh ACC Battery Manufacturing Capacity
articles.description: The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has invited global bids through a Request for Proposal (RFP) to select beneficiaries for establishing 10 GWh of giga-scale Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) manufacturing facilities. MHI shared its plan in a press release to support the development of Grid-Scale Stationary Storage Systems (GSSS) under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for ACC Battery Storage through this tender. The bidding process will be conducted online through a transparent two-stage Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) mechanism on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal. The tender documents have been available since July 15, 2026. A pre-bid conference is scheduled for July 29, 2026. Bids have been invited until October 13, 2026, while the technical bids will be opened on October 14, 2026. In May 2021 , the Union Cabinet approved the PLI Scheme under the National Programme on ACC Battery Storage, with a budgetary outlay of Rs. 18,100 crore to achieve 50 GWh of ACC manufacturing capacity in the country. The scheme aims to reduce India's dependence on imported ACCs by strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and incentivising both domestic and international companies to establish a globally competitive ACC battery manufacturing ecosystem in India. Under the PLI ACC Scheme, planned to add 40 GWh of the targeted 50 GWh manufacturing capacity, which has been awarded to domestic manufacturers. The remaining 10 GWh capacity, earmarked for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage Systems (GSSS), will support the country's growing energy storage requirements driven by rapid renewable energy deployment. Previous Winner of 10 GWh ACC Battery Tender Under the PLI Scheme Previously, the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) announced the selection of the successful bidder under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage. Reliance Industries Limited was awarded 10 GWh of ACC manufacturing capacity through the QCBS mechanism. The ministry said the award marked another step towards enhancing domestic manufacturing capacity, reducing import dependence, and positioning India as a global leader in ACC battery manufacturing. The Ministry of Heavy Industries had received bids from seven companies under the global tender for the rebidding of the 10 GWh Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) manufacturing programme, with a maximum budgetary outlay of Rs. 3,620 crore. The tender was announced on January 24, 2024. According to the ministry, the bidders (in alphabetical order) were ACME Cleantech Solutions Private Limited, Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies Private Limited, Anvi Power Industries Private Limited, JSW Neo Energy Limited, Lucas TVS Limited, Reliance Industries Limited, and Waaree Energies Limited. Together, they bid for a cumulative manufacturing capacity of 70 GWh. All seven bids were evaluated, and six companies were shortlisted for financial evaluation in accordance with the RFP requirements. Subsequently, the financial bids of the qualified bidders were opened on August 2, 2024, following the announcement of the technical evaluation results under the transparent global tender process conducted through the Government of India's CPP Portal. The companies placed on the waitlist under the programme were: ACME Cleantech Solutions Private Limited (Waitlist 1) Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies Private Limited (Waitlist 2) Waaree Energies Limited (Waitlist 3) JSW Neo Energy Limited (Waitlist 4) Lucas TVS Limited (Waitlist 5)

articles.title: Government Invites Global Bids For 10 GWh ACC Battery Manufacturing Capacity
articles.description: Government Invites Global Bids For 10 GWh ACC Battery Manufacturing Capacity New Delhi, Jul 16 (KNN) The Ministry of Heavy Industries has invited global bids for the selection of beneficiaries to establish 10 GWh of giga-scale Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) manufacturing capacity under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for ACC Battery Storage. Global Bids Invited For 10 GWh ACC Capacity The tender, released on July 15, seeks to allocate the remaining 10 GWh capacity under the scheme, which aims to develop a total domestic ACC manufacturing capacity of 50 GWh. So far, 40 GWh has already been awarded to domestic manufacturers. According to the ministry, the pre-bid conference will be held on July 29, while the last date for submission of bids is October 13, 2026. Technical bids will be opened on October 14, 2026, reported PTI. PLI Scheme To Boost Domestic Battery Manufacturing The Union Cabinet had approved the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage in May 2021 with a budgetary outlay of Rs 18,100 crore to promote domestic battery manufacturing and reduce India's dependence on imported ACCs. Focus On Grid-Scale Energy Storage The ministry said the 10 GWh capacity, earmarked for grid-scale stationary energy storage, will support the country's expanding renewable energy capacity by addressing growing energy storage requirements. Initiative To Strengthen Energy Security The initiative is expected to strengthen energy security, reduce import dependence, and help build a globally competitive battery manufacturing ecosystem in India by encouraging investment from both domestic and international manufacturers. (KNN Bureau)

articles.title: How Udyam Registration and Udyam Assist are transforming India’s MSME and entrepreneurial ecosystem
articles.description: New Delhi: India’s entrepreneurial landscape is witnessing a remarkable transformation. As the nation moves towards becoming a global manufacturing and innovation hub, entrepreneurship is emerging as one of the strongest drivers of economic growth, employment generation and inclusive development. Today, millions of individuals are moving beyond the conventional search for jobs and creating enterprises that generate livelihoods for themselves and others. At the centre of this transformation is the Udyam Registration Portal and the Udyam Assist Platform, two landmark digital initiatives of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. These platforms are formalising enterprises, expanding access to Government support and strengthening the MSME ecosystem. Formalising MSME Udyam Registration Portal provides official identity to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises through a simple, paperless, self-declaration-based and free-of-cost online registration process. The Udyam Assist Platform complements this initiative by bringing informal micro enterprises into the formal economy. It enables enterprises that may not yet have GST registration or are not covered under the Income Tax system to receive formal recognition as micro enterprises through verified data submitted by authorised Udyam Assist Partners. Together, these platforms are creating a more inclusive ecosystem by ensuring that even the smallest enterprises can become part of India’s formal economy. Through the Udyam Assist Platform, authorised partners such as banks, NBFCs and other lending institutions help these enterprises obtain formal recognition as Udyam Assist Certificate holders, enabling them to access various Government initiatives meant for micro enterprises. The platform is playing a crucial role in expanding financial inclusion and strengthening grassroots entrepreneurship. Udyam Registration Process The Udyam Registration process has been designed to be quick, transparent and hassle-free. Step 1: Visit the Udyam Registration Portal. Step 2: Enter Aadhaar details of the proprietor, partner or authorised signatory. Step 3: Validate PAN details. Step 4: Fill in enterprise details such as business name, address, bank details and business activities. Step 5: Submit the application through self-declaration. Step 6: Upon successful verification, an e-Certificate with a unique Udyam Registration Number is generated instantly. Also Read: PM Modi’s gift of Uttarakhand Aipan art to Indonesian President reflects India’s rich spiritual and artistic heritage Benefits of Udyam Registration Obtaining Udyam Registration opens the door to a wide range of Government support measures designed to help MSMEs grow. Access to Government Schemes Registered MSME become eligible to avail benefits under various schemes of the Ministry of MSME on finance, technology upgradation, quality certification, skill development, market access and entrepreneurship promotion. Easier Access to Institutional Credit Udyam Registration helps enterprises establish their formal identity, making it easier to approach banks and financial institutions for business loans and credit support. Protection against Delayed Payments Registered MSME can seek protection relating to delayed payments from buyers, helping improve business cash flow. The MSME Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Portal is a digital platform, that facilitates the speedy, transparent, and cost-effective resolution of delayed payment disputes involving Micro and Small Enterprises. The portal enables end-to-end online dispute resolution, from filing a claim to conciliation, arbitration, and final resolution. Participation in Public Procurement Udyam-registered enterprises can participate in Government procurement opportunities and benefit from procurement policies aimed at promoting MSME. Access to Quality and Technology Support MSME can avail assistance for quality certification, technology upgradation, lean manufacturing, digitalisation and productivity enhancement through various Ministry initiatives. Market Promotion Registered enterprises can participate in domestic and international exhibitions, trade fairs and buyer-seller meets organised under different MSME programmes to expand their market reach. Driving Inclusive Growth The combined impact of the Udyam Registration Portal and the Udyam Assist Platform extends beyond business registration. These initiatives are empowering Women, SC/ST entrepreneurs, rural enterprises, traditional artisans, first-generation entrepreneurs and youth-led start-ups by making Government support more accessible and inclusive. By simplifying the registration process and expanding the formal MSME base, these digital platforms are helping transform entrepreneurial aspirations into successful enterprises, contributing significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. Today, more than 8.9 crore enterprises have been registered on the Udyam Registration Portal and Udyam Assist Platform, providing employment to over 38 crore people across the country.
